symptom: ako/mxcli#2094 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1795), follow-up to #2115: after the v1 listing fix, a one-activity `create or modify microflow` still cost 0.35 s per statement on a 3,400-unit project (and 0.06 s on a 1,054-unit v2 one); the profile was ListDomainModels (32%) and ListMicroflows (22%), on v1 and v2 alike.
cause: buildMicroflowFromStmt's entityResolver decoded every domain model of the project on EACH entity lookup (6 full decodes for a flow with two entity parameters and an entity return); the nanoflow and rule builders decoded them all once per build; findMicroflowByQualifiedName decoded every microflow to pick one by qualified name, and `create or modify microflow` calls it per statement.
file: mdl/executor/entity_resolver.go (flowEntityResolver: lazy, GetDomainModel per named module, full listing only as fallback), cmd_microflows_build.go + cmd_rules_create.go (use it; a backend failure is reported, not read as 'entity not found'), calculated_attributes.go (findMicroflowByQualifiedName via microflowsNamed)
insight: Peek the profile's CALLERS of the expensive listing before designing a cache: 73% of ListDomainModels came from one closure and 100% of ListMicroflows from one helper, so two local fixes did what a cross-statement backend memo would, without its invalidation risk (64 and 51 call sites, and the verdict pass applies simulated flow writes, so a pass-wide microflow memo would serve stale flows). Keep the lookup LAZY: listing the modules up front made every build read every module unit on v2 even for flows with no entity type, which TestCheckPasses_ReadEachUnitFileOnce caught (20 reads vs 12). Count backend calls with a wrapper that embeds MockBackend and adds the by-name/by-module methods the mock lacks; the mock's GetDomainModel returns (nil, nil), so the resolver must fall back to the full listing for the other 80-odd mock tests. Measured, OneHarness v1: create or modify 0.86 -> 0.58 s alone, 0.115 s with #2115; check of 150 statements 76 -> 50 s alone, 10 s with #2115; v2 TestApp 0.061 -> 0.020 s.
